### NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
**Question-answered sentence:** A graded-stiffness comb finger design with controlled compliance at the tip to prevent shock-induced contact while maintaining electrostatic sensitivity.

**Standard practice vs. mitigation:** Standard practice uses uniform stiffness comb fingers with fixed geometry, while this intervention introduces a deliberately graded stiffness profile with increased compliance at the tip to absorb shock energy without allowing full finger contact.

**Adjacent-technique clearance:** The closest existing practice is using flexible hinge structures in MEMS devices, but this differs by applying graded stiffness directly to the comb fingers themselves rather than at the structural level, creating distributed compliance where impact is most likely.

**Mechanism:** The graded-stiffness design absorbs shock energy through controlled elastic deformation at the tip, preventing the full transfer of momentum that would cause hard contact and stiction, while maintaining sufficient structural rigidity in the base region to preserve electrostatic sensing capability.

### PHYSICS CHECK
The governing physical relation is the elastic energy absorption: U = ½kδ², where k is the effective stiffness and δ is the displacement. By reducing the effective stiffness (k) at the tip by 50-70% (achievable through geometric tapering), the same shock energy (from 10,000g) causes approximately 2-3× more displacement but with 75-90% lower peak force (F = kδ), preventing the contact pressure threshold for stiction (typically >1 MPa) from being reached. The base region maintains >80% of the original stiffness to preserve electrostatic sensitivity.

### IMPLEMENTATION BILL
**Standard practice components:**
- Uniform-width silicon comb fingers (etch depth: 50μm)
- Fixed electrode gap: 2μm
- Standard photolithography and DRIE processes

**Intervention components:**
- Graded-width silicon comb fingers (etch depth: 50μm, width tapering from 3μm at base to 1μm at tip over last 20μm length)
- Same electrode gap: 2μm (maintained at base region)
- Same photolithography and DRIE processes (no new equipment)
- Additional design step: graded-width mask pattern (CAD modification only)
- No new materials required (same silicon substrate)
- No new instruments required (same fabrication line)
- No new procedures required (same etching parameters)

### BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
| Item | Standard Practice | Intervention | Burden Impact |
|------|-------------------|--------------|---------------|
| Fabrication Equipment | DRIE etcher | Same DRIE etcher | Same |
| Materials | Silicon wafer | Same silicon wafer | Same |
| Lithography | Standard mask | Modified mask (CAD only) | Same |
| Processing Steps | Etch (50μm) | Etch (50μm) | Same |
| Design Complexity | Uniform pattern | Graded pattern | Same (CAD effort) |
| Testing | Standard shock test | Same shock test | Same |
| Overall Burden Class | Standard MEMS process | Standard MEMS process | **Same** |

### EXECUTABLE TEST
**Protocol:** Subject 30 devices (15 control, 15 intervention) to 100g, 500g, 1000g, 5000g, and 10000g shocks along all three axes (5 shocks per axis per device) using a calibrated shock machine with controlled pulse shape (half-sine, 1ms duration). After each shock level, measure zero-g offset using a precision electrostatic force balance system.

**Instruments:** 
- Shock machine with accelerometer feedback (±1% accuracy)
- Precision capacitive readout system (0.1 mg resolution)
- Optical microscope for post-shock inspection

**Pass/Fail Criteria:** 
- Pass: No device shows permanent zero-g offset >50 mg after any shock level
- Pass: No optical evidence of comb finger contact or deformation
- Fail: Any device exceeds 50 mg permanent offset after any shock level

**Duration:** 1 week (including setup, testing, and analysis)

**Kill Criterion:** If >2 devices in either group fail the 1000g shock test, terminate testing and redesign. If >1 device in the intervention group fails at any level, the intervention is falsified.
